facts.claim: Town at the south-eastern end of the Bellarine Peninsula, on the entrance to Port Phillip, south of Swan Bay
Home to Fort Queenscliff and the terminus of the Bellarine Railway

name: Fort Queenscliff

facts.claim: Built from 1860 as an open battery on Shortland's Bluff to defend the entrance to Port Phillip
Headquarters of the chain of forts around Port Phillip Heads; manned as coastal defence 1883-1946
Fort enclosure and museum are visited by guided tour only, about 1.5 hours, starting from the fort gate
Tours run Saturday and Sunday at 11am and 1:45pm, none on public holidays; it is a defence area so bring ID

access_note: Entry by guided tour only, weekends; weekday group tours by booking

facts.claim: Volunteer-run steam tourist railway on a 16 km section of a former branch line between Queenscliff and Drysdale
The Swan Bay Express is a 45 minute train ride departing from Queenscliff Station
The Seaside Explorer runs the longer journey from Drysdale to the coast
Museum in Torquay widely cited as the world's largest surfing and beach culture museum
Includes the Australian Surfing Hall of Fame and surfboards from early wooden boards to modern designs
General admission is self-guided with no time limit

name: Split Point Lighthouse

facts.claim: Lighthouse at Aireys Inlet on the Great Ocean Road, on the Shipwreck Coast
Visitors can climb to the top for 360 degree coastal views, self-guided or on a tour
Known as the 'White Lady' of Round the Twist fame; dolphins or whales may be seen from the balcony

access_note: Children 5 and over only; weather permitting

facts.claim: Town in Surf Coast Shire 21 km south of Geelong, gateway to the Great Ocean Road
Faces Bass Strait; coastal features include Point Danger and Zeally Bay
Home of the Australian National Surfing Museum

name: Great Ocean Road Memorial Arch

facts.claim: A timber-log arch over the Great Ocean Road at Eastern View, between Aireys Inlet and Lorne
It honours the roughly 3,000 returned servicemen who built the road from 1919 to 1932 and W.T.B. McCormack, engineer to the Road Trust
The first arch opened on 4 November 1939; the current arch is a later replacement after the original was lost (sources differ on the date: 1973 or after the 1983 fires)
Tolls were collected at Eastern View from 1922 until the government took over the road in 1936

unresolved: current arch build date: sources conflict (1973 vs after 1983 fires)

name: Erskine Falls

facts.claim: A single-drop waterfall 35.5 m high in the Otway Ranges just outside Lorne
Within Great Otway National Park, about 10 km inland from Lorne via Erskine Falls Road; the access road is steep and unsuitable for caravans
An upper lookout is by the car park; about 240 steps lead down to the base (around 700 m return)
Swimming is not allowed because of unstable rocks and underwater obstacles

access_note: Cora Lynn Cascades track reportedly closed (damaged infrastructure) and lower steps reportedly closed at times; check Parks Victoria

name: Sheoak Falls

facts.claim: A single-tier waterfall 15.8 m high on Sheoak Creek, about 6 km from Lorne
Lies beside the Great Ocean Road in Great Otway National Park

name: Kennett River

facts.claim: A small coastal settlement on the Great Ocean Road between Lorne and Apollo Bay
Grey River Road leads off from the Kafe Koala area; wild koalas are seen in the gum trees along its first couple of kilometres
About 50 koalas were released in the Grey River area in 1977, and counts vary year to year

access_note: Koala sightings not guaranteed; unmade road

name: Cape Otway Lightstation

facts.claim: Victoria's oldest working lighthouse, on Cape Otway; a heritage precinct with historic buildings, cafe and talks
Land-based whale watching is possible from the lighthouse in winter to spring as migrating whales pass close to shore
Self-guided entry; tower climbs are currently unavailable due to heritage conservation works, with limited views in 2026
Accommodation is available on site

access_note: Tower climbs closed for conservation works; adult ticket normally $22, currently discounted to $11 (stored at the normal $22)

facts.claim: An 800 m self-guided circuit walk through cool temperate rainforest in the Otway Ranges near Apollo Bay
Part of Great Otway National Park

name: Hopetoun Falls

facts.claim: A waterfall on the Aire River in the Otways with a single drop of about 18 m.
Reached by a walk in Great Otway National Park; no dogs, camping or fires.
Walk is about 1 km return, roughly 30 minutes (travel guide).

unresolved: No fee stated on the site page; free rests on Victorian national parks not charging entry

name: Triplet Falls

facts.claim: Walk through ancient rainforest to an elevated platform viewing three cascades.
Trail passes a former timber mill site with log carts and other artefacts.
In Great Otway National Park, 70 km from Apollo Bay.
Walk about 1.8 km, roughly 45 minutes (travel guide).

name: Beauchamp Falls

facts.claim: A waterfall about 18.7 m in a single drop, in the Otway Ranges near Beech Forest.
Reached from a picnic and camping area at the end of Beauchamp Falls Road by a walking path of about 3 km return.

name: Otway Fly

facts.claim: A 600 m elevated steel Treetop Walk 25 to 30 m above the forest floor, with a 47 m Spiral Tower and a cantilever over Young's Creek.
Also runs guided 2.5-hour zipline tours between cloud stations in the Otway rainforest.
The Enchanted Forest walk is included with Treetop Walk tickets.

name: Loch Ard Gorge

facts.claim: A gorge framed by limestone cliffs with a sheltered sandy beach, minutes from the Twelve Apostles.
Named for the Loch Ard, wrecked on Mutton Bird Island in 1878; only two of 54 aboard survived, reaching the gorge beach.
Lookouts and short walks around the area; short-tailed shearwaters return to Mutton Bird Island at dusk Oct to Apr.

unresolved: No fee stated on the page; free rests on no entry charge listed

name: Squeaky Beach
bio_draft: Pale quartz sand that squeaks underfoot, in a bay of granite boulders a short walk from Tidal River.

facts.claim: Rounded quartz sand that squeaks underfoot, enclosed by granite boulders at both ends.
Car park and toilets on site, or walk from Picnic Bay or Tidal River.
Not patrolled; beware wave surges and strong currents.

name: The Grotto

facts.claim: The Grotto frames the coastline through a natural window of rock on the Shipwreck Coast
It sits just beyond Port Campbell, near London Bridge and The Arch, off London Bridge Rd
The three stops offer lookouts, sea caves and arches shaped by limestone, wind and waves

access_note: The Arch viewing area next door is closed for unstable cliffs (not The Grotto itself).

name: Bay of Islands

facts.claim: Bay of Islands Coastal Park has ocean-carved cliffs, secluded rock stacks and sheltered bays near Peterborough
It is quieter than nearby big-name Great Ocean Road stops, about 400 km from Melbourne along the road
Sea kayaks can launch from Boat Bay Road at Bay of Islands beach; cliff-top heathland walks have sea views
Southern right whales can be seen off the coast between May and October

access_note: Beaches unpatrolled, not recommended for swimming; limited facilities.
unresolved: No explicit fee statement found; free assumed

facts.claim: Port Campbell is a town on the Great Ocean Road, west of the Twelve Apostles, in the Shire of Corangamite
Whales are often spotted from lookouts along the coast, including Port Campbell township, during migration season
It is the base for the Shipwreck Coast sights

name: Flagstaff Hill Maritime Museum

facts.claim: Flagstaff Hill Maritime Village is in Warrnambool, on Victoria's south-western coast
The museum is built on Flagstaff Hill, which also holds the original lighthouses and Warrnambool Garrison
A sound and light show, Tales of the Shipwreck Coast, runs at dusk (listed on operator booking page)

name: Deep Blue Hot Springs

facts.claim: Deep Blue Hot Springs is a geothermal bathing sanctuary at Worm Bay Road, Warrnambool
It has indoor bath house and outdoor bathing pools; sessions are about two hours
Daytime entry is for ages five and up; evening sessions are adults 16 and over

name: Tower Hill

facts.claim: Tower Hill Wildlife Reserve sits in a large volcanic crater, a dormant volcano near the Great Ocean Road
Emus, kangaroos, koalas, swans and ducks live in the reserve
Walks range from easy boardwalks to the Tower Hill Peak Walk, with the Lava Tongue and Wagon Bay Loop walks
About 15 km north-west of Warrnambool
